messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — HIGH: GPU pool 'g4-pool' at 100% capacity, request queue growing >12m, client throttling detected. Autoscaler failing to add nodes. Paging @ryan_oncall and @sana_platform. :rotating_light:

ryan_oncall: I got the pager. Looking now. First pass: what's the error from cluster-autoscaler?

ops-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scale up failed: failed to launch nodes in nodegroup 'g4-nodegroup-prod' -> LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch, CreateFleetActionDenied (IAM:RunInstances denied)

ryan_oncall: copying relevant logs from CA: 
```
E0901 14:03:12.123456 1 scale_up.go:432] Failed to scale up: failed to create instance: ec2 RunInstances: "Client.UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation"
-- caused by LaunchTemplate version 202 -> desired 205 mismatch
```

ryan_oncall: TL;DR: autoscaler requested new instances but the launch template version referenced by the nodegroup doesn't exist for the account/region (we migrated LT last week), and IAM role used by autoscaler doesn't have permission to use the newer LT. CA is retrying and hitting rate limits.

sana_platform: hmm. We rolled LT 205 to staging only. Production LT 202 is still active, but ASG/eks nodegroup wanted 205 due to a config drift when we updated the machine image. That explains mismatch.

marco_infra: Also seeing a taint mismatch on provisioning: kubelet fails node registration because we require taint gpu:reserved, but new nodes coming up don't get tainted until node bootstrap finishes. Since instances are stuck at RunInstances failure they never reach bootstrap.

ryan_oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) manual ASG scale-up with older LT 202 to get nodes running ASAP; 2) temporarily route traffic to dedciated-standby pool (if capacity available); 3) enable throttled queuing / degrade model to smaller memory footprint. Thoughts?

customer-success-liz: Heads up — two large customers reported timeouts for inference jobs started ~14:00. They see "server busy" errors. We're already fielding tickets.

sana_platform: I'll try manual ASG scale using the existing launch template (202). If that works we get nodes up quickly and take pressure off the queue. Also starting a background job to sync LT versions.

ryan_oncall: OK do that. Post commands you run. I'll prepare a temporary routing change to divert non-critical traffic to dedicated-spot-fallback.

marco_infra: Command to increase ASG desired capacity (run from janitor account):
```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name g4-nodegroup-prod-asg --desired-capacity 6 --honor-cooldown
```

sana_platform: running now. Output: 
```
set-desired-capacity 6
Current capacity 3 -> pending 6
```

ops-bot: AWS: Launch attempt -> RunInstances UnauthorizedOperation (repeat) for new instances in subnet us-west-2a.

sana_platform: hmm aws CLI accepted desired-capacity but EC2 RunInstances still failing because instance creation call references LT 205 via mixed-instance policy. I can patch the ASG to reference template 202. Patching now.

marco_infra: Use this patch to mixed policy JSON: replace LaunchTemplate.Spec.Version = "202" and update ASG. Example: 
```
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name g4-nodegroup-prod-asg --launch-template 'LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd,Version=202'
```

sana_platform: patched. Re-attempting scale up.

ops-bot: cluster-autoscaler: detected increased capacity request, watching for nodes.

ryan_oncall: While nodes come up, I'm enabling a soft-fallback rule: route 20% of inference traffic to model-small fallback and mark non-urgent queues as best-effort. This should reduce pressure. Applying route change.

customer-success-liz: Noted. I'll tell affected customers we have a mitigation and ETA ~20m for new nodes.

sana_platform: New nodes are provisioning. kubelet logs show bootstrap success, taint applied. Node readiness: 2/3 ready so far.

ops-bot: kube events: 
```
Warning FailedScheduling  Pod default/inference-job-xyz  0/120 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient gpu.
Normal NodeHasSufficientMemory  node/i-0abcd Ready
```

ryan_oncall: Good. Keep monitoring queue length. If queue edge still grows, we'll add one-off spot GPU instances via dedicated pool.

marco_infra: Note: CA had also been throttled due to API rate limits caused by many parallel attempts. I bumped CA's --scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m to reduce churn temporarily.

sana_platform: All 3 new nodes ready. Pods starting to schedule. queue backlog dropped from 18m -> 5m in last 7m.

customer-success-liz: Customers reporting improved throughput. Tickets downgraded to P2.

ryan_oncall: Ok triage: root cause = release drift between LaunchTemplate versions + IAM permission gap for autoscaler principal, which prevented RunInstances -> node provisioning. Secondary issue = CA retries + API throttling exacerbated slow recovery.

sana_platform: Post-mitigation steps I'm kicking off: 1) reconcile LT versions across regions and nodegroups; 2) add LT version check to preflight for launches; 3) update CA IAM role to include ec2:RunInstances on all LT versions we may reference; 4) add an alert when ASG desired != LT version used.

marco_infra: I'm opening a follow-up ticket for a one-time inventory sweep of LT versions and image IDs across clusters. Also will add a short cookbook to runbook for manual ASG patching.

ryan_oncall: Handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. @sana_platform please take incident owner for the recovery window and follow-ups. I'll remain reachable if needed.

sana_platform: Taking ownership. Will update the incident playbook and publish postmortem draft.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated — queue growth stopped, GPUs provisioning succeeded, routing rollback to normal starting in 10m.

customer-success-liz: I'll send a customer note summarizing impact and mitigation.

ryan_oncall: Thanks team. Leaving notes: timeline, commands used, ASG patch command, LT reconciliation task. I'll add to postmortem doc when I get back.

sana_platform: Logged runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-autoscale-lt-drift (added remediation checklist).

ops-bot: Incident closed for paging. If any regression happens reopen with /incident reopen <thread_ts>.

sana_platform: Closing thread — continuing follow-ups in #eng-infra.
